title: A finite local algebra over a henselian local ring is henselian
statement: Let R be a henselian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and A a local commutative R-algebra which is finite as an R-module. Then A is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

proof.text: For any finite A-algebra C, transitivity makes C finite over R. The henselian etale retraction theorem and the finite-algebra product-local theorem give an R-algebra isomorphism C with a finite product of local rings C_j. Transport the A-algebra structure along this isomorphism.

Each component C_j is finite over A, since its projection from C is surjective. Its maximal ideal contracts to the maximal ideal n of A. Thus n C_j lies in that maximal ideal and C_j / n C_j is nonzero and local. The quotient C / n C is the product of these quotient rings.

In a local ring an idempotent is zero or one: one of e and 1-e is a unit and e(1-e)=0. Therefore quotient idempotents are zero-one vectors, which lift uniquely to the same vectors in C. The empty product covers C=0. Apply the idempotent/simple-root equivalence and HenselianLocalRing.TFAE to conclude A is henselian.
